stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD with diagonals AC and BD meeting at O. Kavya measures $AC = BD$, $AO = OC$, and $BO = OD$.

Which claim about ABCD is correct?

options.text: ABCD is a rectangle, because its diagonals are equal and bisect each other.
ABCD is a rectangle from $AC = BD$ alone.
The rectangle name is what creates equal bisecting diagonals, so the measurements cannot start the claim.
The same measurements also make any two equal crossing sticks on the desk a rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal diagonals that bisect each other force a rectangle. Equality alone drops bisection. Saying the name creates the diagonals reverses the relation. Extending the rule to loose sticks over-scopes it.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as quadrilateral ABCD with equal bisecting diagonals marked at O.
